title: Just found what might be one of the cheapest real-time financial news APIs
author: bjxxjj
selftext:
I was looking for a cheaper real-time financial news API and came across this:

[tradingnews.press](https://tradingnews.press/)

The pricing caught my attention. Plans start at **$14/month**, and the **$35/month Pro plan includes a real-time WebSocket feed**.

It also looks like it does more than just return raw headlines. The API includes structured fields like:

* related tickers
* urgency level (Breaking / Flash / Regular)
* ticker-level direction / sentiment
* timestamps
* server-side filtering
* deduplicated news events

According to the site, it processes around **5,300 headlines per day** and covers equities, commodities, crypto, and prediction markets 24/7.

Seems potentially useful for algo trading, AI trading agents, or anything that needs to react automatically to breaking market news.

Most real-time financial news APIs I’ve seen are either fairly expensive or clearly aimed at enterprise customers, so **$35/month for real-time streaming + analysis** seemed surprisingly cheap.

Has anyone here tried it?

Or does anyone know of something even cheaper that offers both real-time streaming and structured news analysis?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I haven't used it, so this is a testing checklist and not a review. Before building on any news API, I'd check latency by comparing its timestamps with a wire or exchange source for a few dozen headlines, how "urgency" and "sentiment" are produced (a rule, a model, or a person) and how they perform against what price did next, and whether the timestamps are the publication time or the time the vendor ingested them. Deduplication and coverage claims are easy to test by picking a day and counting what's missing. For the scheduled-event part of the problem (earnings, CPI, FOMC), a calendar with fixed release times is more reliable than parsing headlines, and Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets.
